description: Custom Field Export/Import — Extend jira issue export and import to round-trip custom fields (e.g., Team, Story Points) via field metadata API with automatic name-to-ID resolution

tasks.title: Add NormalizeFieldName and built-in key set to frontmatter.go
tasks.description:
Add two things to `internal/markdown/frontmatter.go`:

1. `func NormalizeFieldName(displayName string) string` — Normalizes a Jira field display name to a YAML-safe key: `strings.ToLower`, replace spaces with underscores, strip all characters not in `[a-z0-9_]` via `regexp.MustCompile("[^a-z0-9_]")`. If result is empty after stripping, return empty string.

2. `var builtinFrontmatterKeys = map[string]bool{...}` — Set of keys reserved by the existing `Frontmatter` struct: `key`, `id`, `type`, `summary`, `status`, `priority`, `labels`, `parent`, `assignee`, `assignee_id`, `reporter`, `reporter_id`, `project`, `created`, `updated`. This is used by export to detect custom-vs-builtin collisions.

3. `func IsBuiltinKey(key string) bool` — returns `builtinFrontmatterKeys[key]`.

No changes to the existing `Frontmatter` struct or `IssueToMarkdown` yet — those come in T-002.
successCriteria: NormalizeFieldName lowercases, replaces spaces with underscores, strips non-[a-z0-9_]
NormalizeFieldName returns empty string for names that normalize to nothing
builtinFrontmatterKeys contains all 15 existing frontmatter YAML keys
IsBuiltinKey returns true for built-in keys, false for custom
Build passes

tasks.title: Add CustomFields to Frontmatter and update IssueToMarkdown
tasks.description:
Modify `internal/markdown/frontmatter.go`:

1. Add `CustomFields map[string]interface{} `yaml:"-"`` to the `Frontmatter` struct (excluded from default YAML marshal).

2. Add custom `MarshalYAML` method on `Frontmatter` that: (a) marshals the struct fields normally via a type alias, (b) unmarshals the result into a `yaml.Node` (mapping node), (c) appends each `CustomFields` entry as additional key-value pairs to the mapping node sorted alphabetically, (d) returns the node. This ensures custom fields appear after built-in fields in YAML output with deterministic order.

3. Change `IssueToMarkdown` signature to `IssueToMarkdown(issue api.Issue, fields map[string]api.Field, warnWriter io.Writer) ([]byte, error)` where `fields` is keyed by field ID (e.g. `customfield_10001`) and `warnWriter` receives warning messages (typically `f.IOStreams.Err`). When `fields` is nil, behavior is unchanged (no custom fields). When `warnWriter` is nil, warnings are silently discarded (use `io.Discard` internally). The `internal/markdown` package is below `factory` in the layer order, so it cannot import `iostreams` — accepting `io.Writer` is the correct pattern.

4. In `IssueToMarkdown`, after setting built-in fields, iterate `issue.Fields.CustomFields` (type `map[string]json.RawMessage`). For each entry: look up the field ID in `fields` map to get the display name, call `NormalizeFieldName(field.Name)` to get the YAML key. Skip + warn to `warnWriter` if: key is empty (field name normalized to nothing), `IsBuiltinKey` returns true (built-in collision), or custom-to-custom name collision (see below). Extract value using `extractCustomFieldValue(raw json.RawMessage) (interface{}, bool)` (new helper). If extraction returns false, skip + warn. Otherwise add to `fm.CustomFields`.

5. Add `extractCustomFieldValue(raw json.RawMessage) (interface{}, bool)` — Determines the YAML value from a `json.RawMessage`. Rules per the plan:
   - Unmarshal into `interface{}`. Check resulting Go type:
   - `string`, `float64`, `bool` → return value, true
   - `nil` → return nil, false (omit)
   - `map[string]interface{}` → try `.value` key first (if string/float64), then `.name` key (if string/float64). If neither exists or value isn't scalar, return nil, false
   - `[]interface{}` (array) → return nil, false
   - Default → return nil, false

6. Handle custom-to-custom name collision: track seen normalized names in a `map[string]string` (normalized→fieldID). If collision, keep first, warn to `warnWriter` with both field IDs.

Update call sites:
- `internal/cmd/issue/export.go:writeFileAtomic` — change `markdown.IssueToMarkdown(issue)` to `markdown.IssueToMarkdown(issue, nil, nil)` temporarily (the real field map and warnWriter come in T-005).
- Any other call sites in test files — update to add `nil, nil` parameters.
successCriteria: Frontmatter.CustomFields is yaml:"-" (excluded from default marshal)
MarshalYAML appends custom fields after built-in fields
IssueToMarkdown accepts fields map + io.Writer for warnings, nil/nil preserves old behavior
extractCustomFieldValue handles string, number, bool, null, object with .value/.name, array
Built-in key collision: custom field skipped, warning to stderr
Custom-to-custom collision: first wins, warning with both field IDs
export.go call site updated to pass nil
Build passes
tasks.notes: This is at the limit of one context window. The MarshalYAML + extractCustomFieldValue + IssueToMarkdown changes are tightly coupled and can't be split without leaving the build broken.

tasks.title: Add tests for NormalizeFieldName, extractCustomFieldValue, and custom field marshaling
tasks.description:
Create or extend `internal/markdown/frontmatter_test.go` with table-driven tests:

1. `TestNormalizeFieldName` — cases: `"Story Points"` → `"story_points"`, `"Team"` → `"team"`, `"Custom Field (v2)"` → `"custom_field_v2"`, `"!!!"` → `""` (empty), `"Already_Normal"` → `"already_normal"`, `"  spaces  "` → `"spaces"`, `"MixedCase123"` → `"mixedcase123"`.

2. `TestIsBuiltinKey` — `"key"` → true, `"summary"` → true, `"team"` → false, `"story_points"` → false.

3. `TestExtractCustomFieldValue` — since the function is unexported, test indirectly via `IssueToMarkdown`. Or if needed, create a `TestExtractCustomFieldValue` in the same package (internal test). Cases per the serialization rules table in the plan: string, number, bool, null (omitted), object with `.value`, object with `.name`, object with neither, array (skipped).

4. `TestIssueToMarkdownWithCustomFields` — Build an `api.Issue` with `CustomFields` map containing several custom field entries (`customfield_10001` → `"Platform"`, `customfield_10002` → `5.0`, `customfield_10003` → `{"value": "Critical"}`). Pass a `fields` map with matching `api.Field` entries. Verify the output YAML contains `team: Platform`, `story_points: 5`, `severity: Critical` after the built-in fields.

5. `TestIssueToMarkdownBuiltinCollision` — Custom field whose normalized name is `"status"` → skipped (not in output). Pass a `bytes.Buffer` as `warnWriter`, verify warning message written to buffer and custom field absent from YAML output.

6. `TestIssueToMarkdownNilFields` — Pass `nil, nil` for fields and warnWriter → no custom fields in output (backward compat).

7. `TestIssueToMarkdownWarnWriter` — Verify that skipped fields (array value, builtin collision) write warnings to the provided `io.Writer`. Verify `nil` warnWriter doesn't panic.

Use existing test patterns from `internal/markdown/frontmatter_test.go`.
successCriteria: NormalizeFieldName tested with 7+ cases including empty result
IsBuiltinKey tested for built-in and custom keys
extractCustomFieldValue tested for all 8 value types from serialization table
IssueToMarkdown with custom fields verified in YAML output
Built-in key collision verified (custom field absent from output, warning in warnWriter)
nil/nil parameters preserve backward compatibility
nil warnWriter doesn't panic
Tests pass

tasks.title: Add custom field unmarshaling to parse.go for import
tasks.description:
Modify `internal/markdown/parse.go` to capture unknown frontmatter keys as custom fields during parsing.

Custom fields go on `Frontmatter.CustomFields` (the `map[string]interface{}` added in T-002), NOT on `IssueFile`. This keeps the data model clean: `Frontmatter` carries both built-in and custom fields.

In `ParseFile`, after the existing `yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(yamlContent), &fm)` (line 67), add a second pass:
1. Unmarshal the same `yamlContent` into `map[string]interface{}`
2. Iterate the raw map keys
3. Check each key against `IsBuiltinKey()` (from `frontmatter.go`, added in T-001)
4. Keys that are NOT built-in go into `fm.CustomFields`
5. If no non-built-in keys found, leave `fm.CustomFields` nil (don't allocate empty map)

No changes to `IssueFile` struct. No changes to `ParseDir`.
successCriteria: ParseFile populates Frontmatter.CustomFields with unknown YAML keys
Built-in keys are NOT duplicated in CustomFields
Existing ParseFile tests still pass (no regressions)
Build passes

tasks.title: Update export command to fetch field metadata and pass to IssueToMarkdown
tasks.description:
Modify `internal/cmd/issue/export.go`:

1. Add `Fields string` to `ExportOptions` — `--fields` flag value (comma-separated list of normalized custom field names, empty = all).

2. Register flag: `cmd.Flags().StringVar(&opts.Fields, "fields", "", "Comma-separated custom field names to include (default: all)")`.

3. In `runExport`, after getting the API client, call `client.ListFields(ctx)` (from `internal/api/schema.go:11`) to fetch all field metadata. Build a `map[string]api.Field` keyed by field ID (e.g. `customfield_10001` → `api.Field{...}`).

4. If `--fields` is set, parse the comma-separated list, normalize each name via `markdown.NormalizeFieldName()`, then filter the field map to only include fields whose `NormalizeFieldName(field.Name)` matches one of the requested names. Warn to stderr for any requested name not found in field metadata.

5. Remove the `exportFields` variable (line 31-34) — instead, pass an empty `Fields` slice to `SearchIssues` (or omit it), which tells Jira to return all fields. Actually, looking at the Jira API behavior: an empty `Fields` slice may return nothing. Check the `SearchOptions` handling — if `Fields: nil` means "all fields", use nil. If not, use `Fields: []string{"*all"}` or similar. The safest approach is `Fields: []string{"*all"}` which Jira interprets as "return all fields".

6. Pass the field map and `f.IOStreams.Err` (as `io.Writer`) to `markdown.IssueToMarkdown(issue, fieldMap, f.IOStreams.Err)` in `writeFileAtomic`.

7. Update `writeFileAtomic` signature to accept the field map and warn writer: `writeFileAtomic(path string, issue api.Issue, fields map[string]api.Field, warnWriter io.Writer) error`. Update the call in the export loop.

8. For `--dry-run`, include the custom field names in the preview output.
successCriteria: --fields flag registered with correct help text
ListFields called once per export run (before pagination loop)
Field map built from ListFields response, keyed by field ID
--fields filters custom fields by normalized name match (case-insensitive: --fields Team matches team)
--fields with unknown name warns to stderr and continues
exportFields variable removed, search requests all fields
writeFileAtomic passes field map to IssueToMarkdown
Build passes

tasks.title: Update import command to resolve custom fields to Jira field IDs
tasks.description:
Modify `internal/cmd/issue/import.go`:

1. In `runImport`, after getting the API client, call `client.ListFields(ctx)` to fetch field metadata. Build a reverse lookup map: `normalizedName → fieldID` by iterating all fields and calling `markdown.NormalizeFieldName(field.Name)` for each.

2. After parsing files and before processing creates/updates, for each `IssueFile` with non-empty `Frontmatter.CustomFields`: iterate the custom field entries, look up each key in the reverse lookup map. If a key can't be resolved to a field ID, return `clierrors.NewValidationError(fmt.Sprintf("unknown frontmatter key %q in %s: not a Jira field", key, issueFile.Path))` with suggestion to check field names or use YAML comments for notes.

3. In `buildCreateFields` and `buildUpdateFields`, inject resolved custom fields. Add a new parameter `customFieldMap map[string]string` (normalizedName → fieldID) to both functions. For each entry in `issueFile.Frontmatter.CustomFields`, look up the field ID via the map, set `fields[fieldID] = value` (value is already the right type from YAML unmarshal — string, float64, bool).

4. Update call sites of `buildCreateFields` and `buildUpdateFields` to pass the resolved map.

5. For `--dry-run`, include the custom fields in the preview output.
successCriteria: ListFields called once per import run
Reverse lookup map built: normalizedName → fieldID
Unresolvable frontmatter keys error with VALIDATION_ERROR and clear message
buildCreateFields injects custom fields by field ID
buildUpdateFields injects custom fields by field ID
Custom field values sent as-is (string, number, bool from YAML)
Build passes
